summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update13.json → valid=true). New direction on persistence/recovery, recorded as a mechanism plus an explicitly unresolved consequence. persistVote writes the vote term and then the candidate identity as two independent stable-store operations (raft.go:2130-2138) over an interface that exposes only per-key Set/Get (stable.go:5-18), so nothing in the captured code makes the pair atomic; and the duplicate branch in requestVote answers from those two keys alone — granting only on identity-byte equality and otherwise returning without a grant, in both cases skipping the log up-to-dateness comparison the first-time path performs before persisting and granting (raft.go:1697-1705). A crash inside that write pair therefore leaves a newer term paired with an earlier term's candidate identity, making the branch reachable for a term in which the node granted nothing and letting that grant carry identity evidence instead of freshness evidence. I deliberately stopped short of a violation claim, conclusion 'unresolved': the harm depends on how quorums divide (any quorum intersects the nodes holding a committed entry, and those voters still apply the log comparison), and whether the window exists at all depends on the store, since the interface permits batching while no supported store implementation is in the captured tree. Counterevidence is preserved: the chosen order still preserves at most one grant per term, the skipped comparison would only have mattered if the node's log advanced past the requester in between, and a committed-entry loss would still have to defeat the quorum/holder intersection. The discriminator is stated for a later run: read whether any supported store makes the pair atomic, and probe with crash injection between the two writes while the node's log has advanced past the earlier candidate.
